AdderVolSource.description: Source provenance of an issuer's idiosyncratic vol estimate.

oneOf.description: Estimated from the issuer's own residual history.

peer_bucket.description: Dotted bucket path used as proxy (e.g. `"IG.EU.FIN"`).

oneOf.description: Supplied directly by the caller at calibration time.

AntiDilutionPolicy.description:
Anti-dilution protection applied to conversion terms.

When dilutive events occur (stock splits, below-market issuances, special
dividends), the conversion ratio is adjusted to protect bondholders from
value erosion.

# Industry Practice

Most convertible bonds use **Weighted Average** anti-dilution, which is
less protective but more issuer-friendly. **Full Ratchet** is mainly seen
in private placements and venture-style convertibles.

oneOf.description:
Full ratchet: conversion price is reduced to the new issue price
regardless of how many shares were issued. Most protective for holders.

Formula: `new_conversion_price = min(current_conversion_price, new_issue_price)`

Broad-based weighted average: conversion price is adjusted based on the
weighted average of the old and new share prices, factoring in the number
of shares. Less dilutive to existing shareholders than full ratchet.

Formula:
```text
new_cp = old_cp × (shares_outstanding + new_money / old_cp)
                 / (shares_outstanding + new_shares_issued)
```

AttributeFilter.description:
Filters on instrument metadata.

All configured conditions are combined with logical AND.

meta.description: Metadata key/value pairs that must all match exactly.

tags.description: Tags that must all be present on the instrument.

AttributionConfig.description:
Optional configuration for attribution runs.

Allows overriding default tolerances and metrics for attribution calculations.

execution_policy.description:
Controls whether attribution's per-factor repricings run in parallel.

Defaults to [`ExecutionPolicy::Serial`] when omitted. Opt into
[`ExecutionPolicy::Parallel`] only when the caller is not already
parallelizing an outer portfolio or batch loop.

metrics.description:
Metrics to compute for metrics-based attribution (optional)
If not provided, a default set will be used

rate_bump_bp.description: Rate bump size in basis points for sensitivities

rounding_scale.description: Rounding scale override (number of decimal places)

strict_validation.description:
Strict validation mode. When omitted, official spec/execution reports
default to `true` so factor pricing errors fail closed instead of
being zeroed into residual. Set to `false` only for diagnostic runs
that must complete with a soft-failed factor.

target_currency.description:
Optional reporting currency for the attribution output.

When supplied and different from the instrument's native pricing
currency, the per-instrument attribution is computed in native
currency and then translated to `target_currency` via
[`crate::translate_to_target_currency`]. The translation:

- converts every aggregate factor amount at `market_t1`'s FX,
- emits a new `fx_translation_pnl` field that captures the FX move
  applied to the opening position (`val_t0 × ΔFX`),
- stamps `meta.fx_policy.target_currency` so downstream consumers know the
  report is in a non-native currency.

When `None` (the default), the attribution stays in
`val_t1.currency()`.

AttributionFactor.description:
Factor types for P&L attribution.

Groups `MarketContext` inputs by their economic role:
- **RatesCurves**: discount_curves + forward_curves
- **CreditCurves**: hazard_curves
- **InflationCurves**: inflation_curves + published inflation_indices
- **Correlations**: base_correlation_curves
- **Fx**: FxMatrix
- **Volatility**: surfaces and declared scalar volatility quotes
- **MarketScalars**: other prices, non-fixing series and dividends

oneOf.description: Inflation curves and published CPI index changes.

AttributionMethod.description:
Attribution methodology for decomposing P&L.

Four methodologies are supported:
- **Parallel**: Independent factor isolation (may not sum due to cross-effects)
- **Waterfall**: Sequential application (guarantees sum = total, order matters)
- **MetricsBased**: Linear approximation using existing metrics (fast but approximate)
- **Taylor**: Sensitivity-based Taylor expansion (first/second order via bump-and-reprice)

oneOf.description:
Independent factor isolation (may not sum due to cross-effects).

Each factor is isolated independently by restoring T₀ values for that
factor while keeping T₁ values for all others. Residual captures
cross-effects and non-linearities.

Sequential waterfall attribution (guarantees sum = total, order matters).

Factors are applied one-by-one in the specified order. Each factor's
P&L is computed with all previous factors at T₁ and remaining at T₀.
Residual is minimal by construction.

Use existing metrics (Theta, DV01, CS01) for approximation.

Linear approximation using pre-computed sensitivities. Fast but less
accurate for large market moves due to convexity effects.

Sensitivity-based Taylor expansion (first/second order).

Computes sensitivities at T₀ via bump-and-reprice, then multiplies by
observed market moves to decompose P&L. Optionally includes second-order
gamma/convexity terms.

BucketWeighting.description:
How bucket factor means are weighted across issuers in the bucket.

DTS (duration-times-spread) is the desk-standard credit-factor weight
(Ben Dor / Barclays): it avoids overweighting tight or short-duration
names. Position risk exposure remains `β × CS01`; DTS does not replace
CS01. [`BucketWeighting::Equal`] is the opt-out for tests and simple
equally-weighted books.

The historical peel weights each date by **contemporaneous** DTS
(`SD × begin-of-period spread` in Returns space, `SD × same-date spread`
in Levels space), so no as-of information enters historical factor
construction. The anchor peel and decomposition use the as-of / current
cross-section DTS. Spread durations are a single per-issuer value across
the window; duration drift within the window is a documented
simplification.

oneOf.description: Equal weight on every non-folded issuer in the bucket.
Weight `i` by `SD_i (years) × s_i (bp)`, normalized within the bucket.

BumpSizeConfig.description:
Per-factor-type bump magnitudes for finite-difference sensitivity engines.

Unknown fields are rejected on deserialization: every field here has a
serde default, so a typo'd key (e.g. `"credit_bp"`) would otherwise be
silently dropped and the bump would silently revert to 1.0.

credit_bp.description: Default credit bump in basis points.

equity_pct.description: Default equity spot bump in percent.

fx_pct.description: Default FX spot bump in percent.

overrides.description: Per-factor overrides that take precedence over factor-type defaults.

rates_bp.description: Default rates bump in basis points.

vol_points.description:
Default volatility bump in vol points (`1.0` = one vol point =
`0.01` absolute vol).

BumpUnits.description: Units for the bump magnitude. These control normalization to fraction or factor.

oneOf.description: Direct factor (1.10 = +10%). Only valid for Multiplicative mode.

Contingent conversion once the share price meets the trigger level
(a percent of the conversion price) over the observation window.

ConversionPolicy.description: Defines how and when conversion can occur.

oneOf.description: Holder may convert at any time (subject to window, if any).

Bond will mandatorily convert on the specified date.

**Modeling scope**: the tree pricer models conversion only at the
single step mapped from this date; early voluntary conversion before
the mandatory date is not modeled. Forced conversion takes precedence
over coincident call/put rights, and the scheduled coupon remains payable.
Holder may convert within a window.
Conversion tied to an external event or condition.

Mandatory conversion with variable delivery ratio (PERCS / DECS / ACES).

At `conversion_date`, the delivery ratio depends on the stock price:
- If `spot <= lower_conversion_price`: ratio = face / lower_price (max shares, loss)
- If `lower < spot <= upper`: ratio = face / spot (variable, delivers face value)
- If `spot > upper_conversion_price`: ratio = face / upper_price (min shares, capped)

# Industry Practice

PERCS (Preference Equity Redemption Cumulative Stock) cap the upside.
DECS (Dividend Enhanced Convertible Stock) have a dead zone between prices.
ACES (Automatically Convertible Equity Securities) are similar to DECS.

**Modeling scope**: the tree pricer models conversion only at the
single step mapped from `conversion_date`; early voluntary conversion
before that date (offered by some mandatory structures) is not modeled.
Forced conversion takes precedence over coincident call/put rights,
and the scheduled coupon remains payable.

lower_conversion_price.description: Lower conversion price (below this, holder receives max shares).

upper_conversion_price.description: Upper conversion price (above this, holder receives min shares).

dilution_events.description:
Historical dilution events that affect the conversion ratio, recorded
in chronological (non-decreasing date) order and applied in that
order. Validation rejects out-of-order events.

price.description: Conversion price (price per share). If not provided, derive from ratio.

ratio.description: Conversion ratio (shares per bond). If not provided, derive from price.

CreditCalibrationDiagnostics.description:
Structured diagnostics attached to every calibrated artifact.

Consumers can programmatically check coverage (e.g. "≥ 95 % of buckets
had ≥ 5 issuers") without parsing free-form log messages.

This struct omits `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` to allow additive
diagnostic fields in future calibration versions.

bucket_sizes_per_level.description:
One entry per hierarchy level: `BTreeMap<bucket_path, member_count>`.
Counts every issuer assigned to the bucket regardless of
[`IssuerBetaMode`]; the same full-membership count gates fold-up.

fold_ups.description:
Log of all fold-up events triggered by insufficient bucket coverage.

**Load-bearing, not purely diagnostic:**
[`decompose_levels`][crate::credit::decomposition::decompose_levels]
reads these records to reconstruct which `(issuer, level)` pairs were
folded during calibration. Stripping or editing them changes
decomposition results.

mode_counts.description:
Count of resolved [`IssuerBetaMode`] values.

Keys are `"issuer_beta"` and `"bucket_only"`.

r_squared_histogram.description: Optional histogram of per-issuer R² values (bucketed as string ranges).

include_per_bucket_breakdown.description:
When true, populate `LevelPnl.by_bucket` for every level. When false,
only `LevelPnl.total` is populated. Defaults to `true`.

include_per_issuer_adder.description:
When true, populate `CreditFactorAttribution.adder_pnl_by_issuer`.
Defaults to `false` to keep payload small for big portfolios.

CreditFactorModel.description:
Fully self-contained credit factor model artifact.

Produced by offline monthly calibration and loaded at startup by attribution,
risk, and vol-forecast consumers. JSON serialization is deterministic:
`serde_json::to_string` followed by `serde_json::from_str` must produce a
byte-identical round-trip.

# Schema version

[`schema`][Self::schema] is deserialized as an exact v1 marker.

# Determinism

Two `CreditFactorModel` values constructed from identical inputs serialize
to byte-identical JSON. This relies on:
- [`issuer_betas`][Self::issuer_betas] sorted by `issuer_id`.
- All maps using `BTreeMap`.
- [`crate::FactorModelConfig`] respecting its own factor ordering.

anchor_state.description: Factor level values at the calibration anchor date.

bucket_weighting.description:
Bucket-mean weighting used at calibration and required at decompose.

[`BucketWeighting::Equal`] artifacts must not be DTS-weighted at
decompose; [`BucketWeighting::Dts`] artifacts rebuild weights from
persisted [`IssuerBetaRow::spread_duration`] × current spread (bp).

diagnostics.description: Structured calibration diagnostics for programmatic coverage checks.

factor_histories.description:
Embedded factor histories (recommended for self-contained artifacts).

`None` indicates an externally-referenced history store.

generic_factor.description: Reference to the generic PC factor series.

issuer_betas.description: Per-issuer beta rows, sorted by `issuer_id` for wire stability.

panel_frequency.description: Regular observation frequency used to annualize variance (`252`/`12`/`4`).

policy.description: Beta regression policy used during calibration.

static_correlation.description:
Correlation estimate retained from covariance calibration.

`config.covariance` is authoritative for both point-in-time risk and
horizon forecasts. Under ridge this correlation precedes the diagonal
ridge addition; under Ledoit-Wolf it is derived from the shrunk
covariance. Combining it with the unregularized `vol_state.factors`
does not generally reconstruct the selected covariance estimator.

use_returns_or_levels.description: Whether calibration peeled a return panel or a raw level panel.

vol_state.description: EWMA or sample vol state at the anchor date.

CreditHierarchicalConfig.description:
Declarative configuration for a calibrated credit-hierarchy matcher.

The matcher emits PC + per-level credit factors with calibrated betas
looked up from `issuer_betas`. `issuer_betas` must be sorted by
`issuer_id` (binary search is used). `hierarchy` defines the level
ordering and dimension keys used to build factor IDs.

dependency_filter.description: Dependency filter; defaults to "any credit-curve dependency".

hierarchy.description: Hierarchy specification (level ordering and dimension keys).

require_issuer_id.description:
Require the [`ISSUER_ID_META_KEY`] meta key on every credit dependency.

When `true`, a credit dependency whose attributes omit the issuer id
is rejected with [`FactorMatchError::MissingRequiredTag`] instead of
being silently downgraded to the PC-only proxy — an absent key is
usually a data-plumbing failure, and the proxy fallback drops both
hierarchy exposure and idiosyncratic risk. Calibrated artifacts set
this to `true`; hand-built configs default to `false` (`serde`
default) so index-proxy workflows without issuer identities keep
working.

CreditHierarchySpec.description:
Ordered list of hierarchy dimensions, broadest → narrowest.

The ordering is significant: factor IDs and beta vectors are indexed
positionally from level 0 (broadest) to `levels.len()-1` (narrowest).

Produced when persisting market data snapshots through serde.

knot_points.description: Time/factor pairs stored on the curve (must already contain origin `(0.0, 1.0)`).

calendar_id.description: Optional registered holiday calendar identifier (`"brbd"`, `"usny+target2"`, etc.).

knot_points.description: Strictly increasing `(time_years, cpi_level)` pillars starting at `0.0`.

knot_points.description: Time/value pairs used to construct the curve

DateRange.description:
A closed calendar-date interval `[start, end]`.

Used to record the history window consumed by calibration.

DateWire.description: ISO 8601 calendar date encoded as a `YYYY-MM-DD` JSON string.

oneOf.description:
1/1 day count convention.

One unit per contractual accrual period, irrespective of its length.

# Standards Reference

- **ISDA**: 2006 ISDA Definitions, Section 4.16(a) - "1/1"

Actual/360 day count convention.

Year fraction = (actual days between dates) / 360

# Standards Reference

- **ISDA**: 2006 ISDA Definitions, Section 4.16(e)
- **ISO 20022**: Day Count Fraction Code "Actual/360" (A004)
- **Also known as**: Act/360, A/360, French

Actual/365 Fixed day count convention.

Year fraction = (actual days between dates) / 365

# Standards Reference

- **ISDA**: 2006 ISDA Definitions, Section 4.16(d)
- **ISO 20022**: Day Count Fraction Code "Actual/365 Fixed" (A005)
- **Also known as**: Act/365F, A/365F, English

Actual/365 Leap day count convention (Actual/365L).

Year fraction = (actual days) / (365 or 366). Requires the enclosing
calculation period (`coupon_period`); no frequency is used. The
denominator is 366 if that period's end date is in a leap year, else
365, for every coupon frequency. Not Actual/Actual AFB.

# Standards Reference

- **ISDA**: 2006 ISDA Definitions as amended, 2021 ISDA Definitions
  section 4.6.1(ix); ISDA's October 2022 GLEIS response (A009)
- **ISO 15022**: Day Count Fraction Code "Actual/365L" (A009)
- **Also known as**: Act/365L, Actual/365 Leap

Fixed US 30U/360 EOM day count convention.

30-day months over a 360-day year; a day-31 or February month-end
start becomes 30, and the end's February month-end becomes 30 only
when the start is also February month-end. Not `30/360 PSA`.

# Standards Reference

- **QuantLib**: `Thirty360::USA`
- **Also known as**: 30U/360 EOM

30/360 ISDA bond basis day count convention.

30-day months over a 360-day year; a day-31 start becomes 30, and a
day-31 end becomes 30 when the adjusted start is 30. No February rule.

# Standards Reference

- **ISDA**: 2006 ISDA Definitions, Section 4.16(f) - "30/360"
- **QuantLib**: `Thirty360::BondBasis` (also `Thirty360::ISMA`)
- **Also known as**: 30/360 bond basis

30E/360 (Eurobond Basis) day count convention.

30-day months over a 360-day year; day 31 becomes 30 at both ends, with
no February adjustment.

# Standards Reference

- **ISDA**: 2006 ISDA Definitions, Section 4.16(g) - "30E/360"
- **QuantLib**: `Thirty360::European`
- **Also known as**: 30/360 European, Eurobond Basis

30E/360 (ISDA) day count convention.

30-day months over a 360-day year; the last day of any month, including
February, becomes 30, except a February month-end end date that is the
termination date. Requires an explicit `end_is_termination_date`.

# Standards Reference

- **ISDA**: 2006 ISDA Definitions, Section 4.16(h) - "30E/360 (ISDA)"
- **QuantLib**: `Thirty360::ISDA` (with its termination date)
- **Also known as**: 30E/360 ISDA, German

30/360 Italian day count convention.

30-day months over a 360-day year; day 31 becomes 30, and any February
day after the 27th becomes 30.

# Standards Reference

- **QuantLib**: `Thirty360::Italian`
- **Also known as**: 30/360 Italian

NL/365 (Actual/365 No Leap) day count convention.

Year fraction = (actual days excluding any February 29) / 365

# Standards Reference

- **Also known as**: Act/365 No Leap, NL365, Actual/365NL

Actual/Actual (ISDA) day count convention.

Actual days over the actual days in the containing calendar year,
split and summed across year boundaries.

# Standards Reference

- **ISDA**: 2006 ISDA Definitions, Section 4.16(b) - "Actual/Actual (ISDA)"
- **ISO 20022**: Day Count Fraction Code "Actual/Actual ISDA" (A006)
- **Also known as**: Act/Act (ISDA), Actual/Actual, Act/Act

Actual/Actual (ICMA) day count convention.

Actual days over (actual days in the coupon period × coupons per year).
Requires an ICMA coupon frequency (`1M`, `2M`, `3M`, `4M`, `6M`, `12M`,
`1Y`) and the enclosing unadjusted nominal `coupon_period`.

# Standards Reference

- **ICMA**: ICMA Rule Book, Rule 251 - "Actual/Actual (ICMA)"
- **ISO 20022**: Day Count Fraction Code "Actual/Actual ICMA" (A007)
- **Also known as**: Act/Act (ICMA), Act/Act (ISMA), ISMA-99

Actual/Actual AFB day count convention.

Whole years counted backwards from the end date, plus a residual of
actual days over 366 if it contains February 29, else 365.

# Standards Reference

- **QuantLib**: `ActualActual::AFB`
- **AFB**: Association Française des Banques master agreement definitions
- **Also known as**: Actual/Actual Euro, Act/Act AFB

Business/252 day count convention.

Year fraction = (business days between dates) / 252. Requires a holiday
calendar.

# Standards Reference

- **ANBIMA**: standard for BRL-denominated instruments
- **Also known as**: BUS/252, Business/252

DayCountContextState.description:
Serializable snapshot of [`DayCountContext`] state for persistence and interchange.

This struct captures the optional context parameters (calendar, frequency, business-day basis)
needed to reconstruct a [`DayCountContext`] at runtime using the built-in calendar lookup.
`Default` is the empty context (no calendar, frequency, basis, coupon
period or termination status), the snapshot of
[`DayCountContext::default`].

bus_basis.description: Optional custom business-day divisor (defaults to 252 when `None`).

coupon_period.description:
Optional unadjusted regular ICMA reference period or ACT/365L enclosing
coupon `(start, end)`, serialized as two ISO dates.

Required for exact ICMA accrual on round-trip. `None` selects the
frequency-only ICMA calculation path; ACT/365L requires these dates.

end_is_termination_date.description:
Whether the later accrual endpoint is the contractual termination
date; `None` (omitted or `null` on the wire) means unspecified, which
30E/360 ISDA rejects.

frequency.description: Optional coupon frequency, required for ACT/ACT ISMA.

DecimalWire.description:
Exact decimal encoded only as a JSON string.

Restoration routes through [`crate::decimal::parse_decimal`], the single
exact text-admission rule: JSON numbers, malformed text and inexact values
are rejected rather than rounded. Serialization writes canonical
fixed-point text with trailing zeros removed and signed zero normalized
(`"1.5"`, `"0"`), never scientific notation.

oneOf.description: SDA standard curve: ramps to peak then declines

Explicit annual CDR for each month of seasoning; the last value is
held for later months.

monthly_cdr.description: Annual CDR per month of seasoning as decimals, month 1 first.

oneOf.description:
Cumulative net loss curve (rating-agency ABS convention): losses as a
percent of the original pool balance by month of seasoning, with a
constant loss severity. Defaults in month `t` are
`Δloss_t / severity` of the original balance; see
[`DefaultModelSpec::mdr_with_survival`] for the conversion to a
monthly rate on the surviving balance. Cumulative defaults may exceed
the original balance after replenishment or par build.

cumulative_net_loss_pct.description:
Cumulative net loss in percent of the original balance per month
of seasoning (`1.5` = 1.5%), non-decreasing, month 1 first; the
last value is held.

severity.description: Loss severity as a decimal fraction of defaulted par in `(0, 1]`.

oneOf.description:
Rating-agency default timing: a lifetime cumulative default rate
spread over the years of the pool's life. Defaults within a year
accrue linearly by month.

annual_pct.description:
Share of lifetime defaults occurring in each year of seasoning, in
percent (e.g. `[15, 30, 30, 15, 10]`); must sum to 100.

cumulative_default_rate.description: Lifetime defaults as a decimal fraction of the original balance.

DependencyFilter.description: Filters on an individual market dependency.

curve_type.description:
Specific curve role that the dependency must match, when present.

This is only evaluated for curve-like dependencies.

dependency_type.description: Dependency classification that the dependency must match, when present.

id.description:
Exact dependency identifier that must match, when present.

FX pairs use the canonical `BASE/QUOTE` form, for example `USD/EUR`.

DependencyType.description: Classification used by dependency filters and declarative matching config.

DilutionEvent.description:
A dilutive event that triggers anti-dilution adjustment.

Records details of an equity issuance or corporate action that may
affect the conversion ratio under the bond's anti-dilution provisions.

new_issue_price.description: New issue price per share (for below-market issuances).

shares_outstanding_before.description: Number of shares outstanding before the event.

DiscountCurveTransform.description:
Source interpolation and a single accumulated transformation, never a chain
of nested curves. The adjustment is stored as its piecewise-linear derivative
so evaluating beyond a completed triangular shock does not subtract large
quadratic polynomials.

adjustment.description: Cumulative derivative of the additive log-factor adjustment.

source_base_date.description: Original, untransformed curve base date defining the source coordinate system.

DividendAdjustment.description:
How dividends affect conversion terms (dividend protection).

Dividend protection compensates the holder for dividends paid on the
underlying, which otherwise leak value from the conversion option (the
stock drifts at `r - q` under the risk-neutral measure). The variants
carry no threshold parameter, so protection is **full**: the entire
continuous dividend yield `q` is protected.

# Pricing model (continuous-yield accretion)

Under the continuous dividend yield `q` used by the tree pricer, each
protected dividend payment bumps the conversion ratio by the dividend
fraction; the continuous limit is exponential accretion from the
valuation date:

```text
AdjustRatio:  ratio(t)  = ratio_0 * exp(q * t)
AdjustPrice:  K_conv(t) = K_0 * exp(-q * t)
```

Since `ratio = notional / K_conv`, the price decay is mathematically the
same ratio accretion — the pricer implements both variants through the
single ratio-accretion mechanism. Accretion composes multiplicatively on
top of any anti-dilution adjustments from
`ConvertibleBond::effective_conversion_ratio`.

# Examples

```rust
use finstack_quant_valuations_core::instruments::{AntiDilutionPolicy, ConversionPolicy, ConversionSpec, DividendAdjustment};

let conversion = ConversionSpec {
    ratio: Some(25.0),
    price: None,
    policy: ConversionPolicy::Voluntary,
    anti_dilution: AntiDilutionPolicy::None,
    dividend_adjustment: DividendAdjustment::AdjustRatio,
    dilution_events: Vec::new(),
};
assert!(conversion.dividend_adjustment.is_protected());
```

oneOf.description: Adjust conversion price downward by the dividend amount.
Adjust conversion ratio upward to compensate for dividends.

DividendEvent.description: One gross cash distribution per entitled share on its schedule's share basis.

DividendSchedule.description: Validated distributions for one security, share basis and currency.

ExecutionPolicy.description:
Controls where attribution repricing work spends parallelism.

`Serial` is the default: typical standalone factor sets are small enough
that inner Rayon costs more than it saves. `Parallel` opts into Rayon for
independent factor repricings when the caller is not already parallelizing
an outer portfolio or batch loop.

oneOf.description: Use Rayon for independent attribution repricings.

ExtrapolationPolicy.description:
Extrapolation policy for evaluation outside the knot range.

Every interpolation strategy honours this policy at both ends of the knot
range. Callers must choose an explicit policy:

- `Flat`: hold the boundary ordinate constant outside the knot range
  (and return derivative `0.0` strictly outside the knot range).
- `Extend`: extend the boundary segment's slope in the interpolation style's
  working space (table below).
- `Error`: refuse to extrapolate; return an explicit error for queries
  outside `[knots[0], knots[last]]`.

What `Extend` extends depends on the [`InterpStyle`]:

| Style | `Extend` extends | On a discount-factor curve | On a rate-valued curve |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Linear` | the value linearly | - | rates keep trending |
| `CubicHermite` | the value linearly, with the end-knot slope | - | rates keep trending |
| `LogLinear` | `ln(value)` linearly | flat forward rate | - |
| `PiecewiseQuadraticForward` | `ln(value)` linearly | flat forward rate | - |
| `MonotoneConvex` | the boundary instantaneous forward | flat forward rate | - |

The market-standard tail for a discount-factor curve is a flat forward
rate (`Extend` with a log-space style). For a curve that stores rates or
spreads, holding the last rate constant is `Flat`.

working space; see the table on [`ExtrapolationPolicy`].

FactorCorrelationMatrix.description:
Static factor correlation matrix `ρ` for the covariance decomposition
`Σ(t) = D(t) · ρ · D(t)` where `D(t)` is the diagonal vol matrix.

`factor_ids` defines the row/column ordering; `data[i][j]` is
`ρ_{factor_ids[i], factor_ids[j]}`. The matrix must be square, symmetric,
and have unit diagonal.

FactorCovarianceMatrix.description:
User-supplied factor covariance matrix with row-major storage.

The factor ID order is part of the contract: row `i`, column `j`
corresponds to `factor_ids[i]` and `factor_ids[j]`.

# Units contract

Entries are **annualized (co)variances of factor moves expressed in each
factor's canonical bump unit** — the same unit the sensitivity engines use
for deltas (see [`crate::BumpSizeConfig`] / [`crate::FactorType::bump_units`]):
basis points for rates/credit/inflation, percent for equity/commodity/FX,
vol points for volatility. With sensitivities `s` in P&L-per-canonical-unit
and `Σ` in canonical-unit², `sᵀΣs` is directly an annual P&L variance.
Mixing conventions — e.g. a covariance in decimal² (`0.0001²` per bp²)
against per-bp sensitivities — mis-scales portfolio variance by `1e8`.
The credit calibrator produces matrices in this convention from the spread
panel's native units; hand-built matrices must match it.

data.description:
Annualized (co)variances in row-major order, `n * n` entries, each in
its factors' canonical bump units squared. The matrix is symmetric, so
`data[i * n + j]` equals `data[j * n + i]`.

factor_ids.description: Factor identifiers, in the row and column order of `data`.

the stored values are already period moves; under
[`PanelSpace::Levels`]
they are peeled levels and must be first-differenced before vol or P&L.

FoldUpRecord.description:
Record of a single fold-up event during calibration.

Fold-up means **omit the sparse child factor** and set `β_k = 0` at that
level. The issuer already sits in the parent bucket, so its residual
continues to contribute to the parent mean. This is not a re-tagging of
the issuer into a different leaf.

# Where the folded risk lands

No factor is re-assigned: the variation the sparse bucket's factor would
have carried stays in each member's residual and flows into the
per-issuer **adder** (idiosyncratic) vol. Members of the same folded
bucket therefore share a common component that Σ represents as
*uncorrelated* idiosyncratic risk — holding several names from one folded
bucket overstates diversification for that component. Lower the level's
[`BucketSizeThresholds`][crate::credit::calibration::BucketSizeThresholds]
entry if that correlation materially matters for a thin bucket.

folded_to.description:
Deepest surviving ancestor bucket path (e.g. `"IG.EU"`), recorded for

bucket's factor — the parent level was already peeled at `k − 1`; the
sparse bucket's own variation moves into the issuer adder instead.

reason.description: Human-readable reason for the fold-up (e.g. `"fewer than 5 issuers"`).

betas.description:

For `IssuerBeta` mode, each level loading is the with-intercept OLS
slope of the issuer residual on the **leave-one-out** bucket mean.
Peel and stored factor histories use the **full-bucket** mean, so
the level identity `S_i = β g + Σ β_k L_k + adder` has no drift term.

Equal-weighted artifacts still store the supplied duration (or `1.0`

`levels[i]` is the loading on the bucket factor at hierarchy level `i`.

For `BucketOnly` issuers every component is `1.0` by convention.

# The `0.0` level-beta sentinel

`levels[i] == 0.0` marks a level that was **folded** during calibration
(the issuer's bucket was below the size threshold). The matcher and
`enumerate_factor_ids` skip such levels. A *fitted* beta of exactly `0.0`
is indistinguishable from the sentinel, and that is deliberate: every
consumer scales by the beta (exposure `= β·CS01`, stress shift `= β·shock`,
attribution `= β·ΔL`), so skipping the level and emitting a zero-beta
entry produce identical numbers. The degenerate-regressor guard in
calibration additionally maps near-zero-information fits to the unit-beta
fallback rather than to `0.0`.

Annualization used for sample/EWMA variance and Ledoit-Wolf covariance
is derived from this enum (`252` / `12` / `4`). There is no free

be absent). Annualizes with the market-standard 252.

The grid check accepts any strictly increasing weekday series whose
consecutive gaps are at most 7 calendar days, tolerating weekends and
holiday closures up to a full week. It does not attempt to distinguish
a weekly weekday series from a daily one — the frequency label is a
caller contract, and mislabeling it mis-scales every annualized

CMBS-style lockout: zero prepayment for an initial period, then constant CPR.

PriceTrigger.description:
Share-price trigger of a convertible bond: the last sale price must be at
least `threshold_pct` of the conversion price on `required_days_above` of
`observation_days` consecutive trading days.

Used for the issuer's soft call (`ConvertibleBond::soft_call_trigger`) and
the holder's contingent conversion
(`ConversionPolicy::UponEvent(ConversionEvent::PriceTrigger(..))`).

# Industry Practice

The standard trigger is 130% of the conversion price on 20 of 30
consecutive trading days; some issues use 120% or 150%.

# Modeling scope

The tree evaluates the trigger on the instantaneous node spot. The soft
call applies a Broadie-Glasserman-Kou-style barrier shift scaled by
`required_days_above / observation_days`; contingent conversion compares
the node spot with the nominal level and does not model the observation
window.

observation_days.description: Number of trading days in the observation window (e.g., 30).

required_days_above.description:
Minimum number of days within the window on which the share price
must be at or above the level (e.g., 20 of 30).

threshold_pct.description:
Trigger level as a percent of the conversion price (`130.0` = 130%);
must exceed 100.

RateQuoteBinding.description: Identity and resolved maturity of a quote in its original evaluator.

pillar_time.description: Curve-clock year fraction at the resolved maturity.

rate.description: Recovery rate as fraction (0.0 to 1.0, e.g., 0.40 for 40%)

severity_vector.description:
Loss severity (`1 − recovery`) by month of default as decimals in
`[0, 1]`, month 1 first; the last value is held. When present it
replaces `rate` for defaults in that month.

RiskMeasure.description: Risk measure used when aggregating factor exposures.

oneOf.description: Aggregate exposures using factor covariance and portfolio variance.

Aggregate exposures using Value at Risk at a fixed one-sided loss confidence level.

This assumes the downstream aggregation engine is interpreting the factor
model as a parametric, one-period loss distribution rather than a full
historical or Monte Carlo simulation.

# Sign convention

VaR is reported as a **negative** number on the P&L axis: for a long-risk
portfolio, `total_risk` at 99% is approximately `-sigma * z_{0.99}`.
Factor contributions carry the same sign as the total. Downstream
aggregators and visualizations rely on this convention.

confidence.description: Confidence level in the open interval `(0.5, 1)`.

oneOf.description:
Aggregate exposures using expected shortfall at a fixed one-sided loss confidence level.

As with [`Self::VaR`], this is intended for parametric factor-model
aggregation rather than full-path simulation, and ES is reported as a
**negative** number using the P&L sign convention.

confidence.description: Confidence level in the open interval `(0.5, 1)`.

SabrParameterData.description:
Data-only SABR parameters for one volatility-cube node.

This type records calibrated market data. SABR evaluation, interpolation,
calibration, and convention conversion are owned by
`finstack-quant-models`.

beta.description: CEV exponent in the closed interval `[0, 1]`.

nu.description: Volatility of volatility, nonnegative; zero is the deterministic-volatility limit.

rho.description: Forward-volatility correlation in the open interval `(-1, 1)`.

shift.description: Optional finite displacement applied to forward and strike.

SchemaVersion.description: Numeric schema revision for contracts whose sole supported revision is v1.

Seniority.description:
Seniority level for credit exposures.

Order is **not** total — `SeniorSecured` is strictly senior to `Senior`,
`Subordinated`, and `Junior`, but the relative ordering of `Subordinated`
vs. `Junior` is jurisdiction-dependent. Do not rely on `Ord` semantics.

SeriesExtrapolation.description:
Right-tail extrapolation policy for [`ScalarTimeSeries`].

Applies only to dates strictly after the latest observation; queries on an
empty series or strictly before the earliest observation always fail.

oneOf.description: Hold the latest observed value flat after the final observation date.
Return an error when querying strictly after the final observation date.

credit_spread_bump_bp.description: Credit spread bump size for CS01 computation (basis points).

rate_bump_bp.description: Rate bump size for DV01 computation (basis points).

vol_bump.description: Vol bump size for vega computation (absolute vol points, e.g. 0.01 = 1%).

count.description:
Number of `unit` periods in the tenor. Must be at least 1; `0` is
rejected because a zero-length period makes schedule generation loop.

unit.description:
Calendar unit the count is expressed in, such as days, weeks, months,
or years.

UnmatchedPolicy.description:
Policy for handling dependencies that do not match any factor.

Serializes in `snake_case`, matching the crate-wide wire convention and
this type's own `Display` representation.

oneOf.description:
Fail immediately when any dependency is unmatched.

Use this in production risk runs where dropping unmapped risk would be a
control failure.

Continue but surface a warning to the caller.

Suitable for exploratory workflows where visibility matters but a hard
failure would be too disruptive.

VolCube.description:
SABR volatility cube on an expiry x tenor grid.

Each grid node stores a [`SabrParameterData`] and a forward rate. The
interpolation mode records how a models-layer evaluator should combine
nodes; core performs structural validation only.

expiries.description: Option expiries in years, strictly increasing. Indexes the first axis.

id.description: Identifier the cube is registered and looked up under.

interpolation_mode.description: How volatilities are interpolated between the cube's grid points.

tenors.description:
Underlying swap tenors in years, strictly increasing. Indexes the
second axis.

oneOf.description:
Interpolate implied volatility directly.

This is the literal choice when market quotes are given as implied
volatilities on the stored grid and you want local interpolation in
quote space.

# ⚠️ Not calendar-arbitrage-safe across expiry

Linear-in-vol interpolation along the **expiry** axis does not preserve
monotonicity of total variance `σ²·t`, so an off-grid vol read between
two expiry pillars can imply *decreasing* total variance with time —
i.e. calendar arbitrage — even when the pillar grid is itself
arbitrage-free. For arbitrage-sensitive workflows (Dupire local vol,
no-arb checks, term-structure interpolation) select
[`TotalVariance`](Self::TotalVariance) via
[`VolSurfaceBuilder::interpolation_mode`].

Interpolate total variance `sigma^2 * t`, then convert back to implied vol.

Preferred when blending across expiries: total variance behaves more
linearly in time and preserves the no-arbitrage intuition for variance
accumulation, avoiding the calendar-arbitrage trap of linear-in-vol
interpolation (see [`Vol`](Self::Vol)).

VolQuoteType.description:
Quoting convention of the volatilities stored on a [`VolSurface`].

The same `vol_surface_id` channel is read by consumers with very different
expectations: rates calibrations typically read normal (Bachelier, absolute)
vols on an `expiry × tenor` ATM matrix, while equity/FX/swaption smile
consumers read Black (lognormal, relative) vols on `expiry × strike`. The
stored numbers are an order of magnitude apart (e.g. 0.008 normal vs 0.20
Black), so misreading one as the other silently mis-prices. Tagging the
quote type lets consumers enforce their convention via
[`VolSurface::require_quote_type`].

oneOf.description: Black (lognormal) implied volatility in relative units per square-root source year.
Displaced Black volatility; one per-expiry displacement accompanies the grid.
Normal (Bachelier) implied volatility in underlying units per square-root source year.

VolState.description:
Complete vol state for all factors and all issuers at the calibration date.

Records unregularized per-factor variance estimates and drives per-issuer
idiosyncratic volatility forecasts. Systematic covariance forecasts scale
the calibrated covariance, preserving the selected covariance estimator.

factors.description:
EWMA or sample vol model for each systematic factor.

Keys are factor IDs from [`crate::FactorModelConfig`].
`BTreeMap` for deterministic serialization order.

idiosyncratic.description:
Idiosyncratic vol model for each issuer.

`BTreeMap` for deterministic serialization order.

VolSurface.description:
Volatility surface defined on an expiry × secondary-coordinate grid.

Internally stores annual volatilities in row-major order as a boxed slice.

displacements.description: Additive displacements in forward/strike units, one per expiry for shifted Black quotes.

expiries.description: Strictly positive option expiry times in years.

expiry_clock.description: Optional calibration clock mapping calendar dates to source expiry year fractions.

secondary_axis.description: Semantic meaning of the secondary axis.

secondary_values.description: Secondary-axis coordinates (absolute strikes or positive underlying tenors).

VolSurfaceAxis.description:
Semantic meaning of the secondary axis on a [`VolSurface`].

Most option surfaces are defined on `expiry × strike`, but some calibration
workflows materialize ATM matrices on `expiry × tenor`. Keeping the axis type
explicit prevents consumers from accidentally interpreting tenor buckets as
strikes.

oneOf.description: The secondary axis is literal absolute strike in underlying units.
The secondary axis is strictly positive swap or reference tenor in years.

day_count.description: Day-count convention used to measure expiry times from `reference_date`.

reference_date.description: Valuation reference date anchored to year fraction `0.0`.

description: Shared market snapshots, dates, method and options for a batch of instruments

credit_factor_detail_options.description:
Detail/payload options for `credit_factor_detail`. Inert when
`credit_factor_model` is `None`.

credit_factor_model.description:
Optional calibrated credit factor model. When present (and the
instrument has a recognizable issuer + credit-curve exposure), the
returned `PnlAttribution` carries a `credit_factor_detail` field with
generic / per-level / adder P&L additively decomposing
`credit_curves_pnl`. Parallel and waterfall populate the detail via
the reprice cascade; metrics-based and Taylor back-solve it after
the linear decomposition.

full_cross_attribution.description: Option to compute all 36 cross-factor pairs when enabled

model_params_t0.description: Optional model parameters at T₀ (for attributing parameter changes)
